channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Singapore Is ‘Very Disappointed’ by Trump’s Proposed Tariff Hike
item.description: Singapore said it disagrees with the US findings that the city-state’s policies contribute to excess manufacturing capacity and will urge Washington to reconsider proposed tariffs of up to 20% on its exports.
item.dc:creator: Philip J. Heijmans

item.title: Kim Jong Un Makes Rare Show of Nuclear Warheads After Snubbing Trump Talks
item.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected atomic warheads and a plant making fissile material for bombs, pledging never to waver from his country’s status as a nuclear-armed state after snubbing President Donald Trump’s overtures for talks.
item.dc:creator: Soo-Hyang Choi

item.title: Breaking Down US Plans For New Tariffs
item.description: The US has announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies under President Donald Trump’s push to restore sweeping global import taxes that the Supreme Court found unconstitutional. United States Studies Centre Economic Security Director Hayley Channer weighs the risks behind the move. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Brazil Lashes Out at New US Tariffs, Saying It Will ‘Not Yield’
item.description: The US decision to impose new tariffs on Brazil provoked a sharply worded response from the country’s government, which vowed it would “not yield to this kind of threat.”
item.dc:creator: Augusta Saraiva and John Harney

item.title: Vance: Don’t Think Jensen Huang Needs a Pardon
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Decision Tree Research Founder and CEO Gregory Allen says Jensen Huang should expect intense scrutiny from both Democrats and Republicans when the Nvidia CEO testifies on Capitol Hill next week. Former White House Acting Chief of Staff Mick Mulvaney says President Donald Trump appears out of touch with voters in his handling of the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. American Action Forum President Douglas Holtz-Eakin says a half-point Federal Reserve rate hike would send an important message that policymakers are serious about returning inflation to target. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Houthis Launch Retaliatory Attacks on Two Saudi Ports on Red Sea
item.description: Yemen’s Houthis carried out strikes on Saudi Arabia’s Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan Wednesday, as the Iran-backed militants and the kingdom continue to exchange fire with no signs of respite.
item.dc:creator: Sherif Tarek

item.title: Holtz-Eakin: 50bps Hike Would Send ‘Important Message’
item.description: American Action Forum President Douglas Holtz-Eakin says a half-point Federal Reserve rate hike would send an important message that policymakers are serious about returning inflation to target. The former Congressional Budget Office director says, however, tariffs and market volatility could ultimately lead the Fed to opt for a quarter-point move instead. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Mulvaney: Trump ‘Reading the Room Wrong’ on Huang
item.description: Former White House Acting Chief of Staff Mick Mulvaney says President Donald Trump appears out of touch with voters in his handling of the controversy surrounding Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. Mulvaney says the administration’s response risks fueling anti-Republican sentiment and predicts Huang will probably receive a presidential pardon. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Allen: Huang to Face ‘Full Firepower’ on Capitol Hill
item.description: Decision Tree Research Founder and CEO Gregory Allen says Jensen Huang should expect intense scrutiny from both Democrats and Republicans when the Nvidia CEO testifies on Capitol Hill next week. Allen, a former Pentagon AI policy official, says Huang’s return to Nvidia has also strengthened lawmakers’ momentum for tighter chip export controls. He speaks with Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Nasdaq Bounces Back
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
On today’s episode:
Michael Ball, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist & Jess Menton, Bloomberg News US Equities Team Lead Ian King, Bloomberg Semiconductor Reporter Gautam Mukunda, Bloomberg Opinion Columnist Kate Krader, Bloomberg Pursuits Food Editor (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Hong Kong Fire Shows Accountability Under Beijing’s Shadow
item.description: In late October, Hong Kong leader John Lee sat before scores of journalists to unveil a report on the city’s worst fire in decades — a display that underscored both how much the former British colony has shifted toward mainland China, and how it remains distinct.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Choong Wilkins and Nectar Gan

item.title: Nasdaq 100 Bounces Off Tech-Driven Lows
item.description: The Nasdaq 100 Index trimmed losses that had briefly tipped the gauge into bear-market territory and the S&P erased most of an earlier large decline, with dip buyers emerging even as doubts remained about the outlook for artificial intelligence. The Russia/Ukraine War is testing NATO’s plan for military action. Plus, Trump is targeting China, EU with new tariffs citing overcapacity. All on the latest episode of “Bloomberg Businessweek Daily.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Inside Hong Kong's Deadly Fire
item.description: On November 26, 2025, Hong Kong firefighters were called to Wang Fuk Court, a complex of eight 31-story residential towers. What followed was the city’s deadliest fire in almost eight decades, an inferno that claimed 168 lives and triggered a year of recriminations over who was at fault. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: The Rising Cost of Thanksgiving, From Travel to Turkey
item.description: Even before Americans sit down at the table, they’re paying more than before.
item.dc:creator: Julia Fanzeres

item.title: Judge Clears New York Rent Freeze Backed by Mayor Mamdani
item.description: A rent freeze backed by New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani’s administration was cleared by a state judge who dismissed a lawsuit filed by a group of landlords seeking to void the measure, which went into effect last month.
item.dc:creator: Chris Dolmetsch

item.title: Trump Revives US Tariff Regime
item.description: On the early edition of Balance of Power, Bloomberg Washington Correspondents Joe Mathieu discusses the latest from DC. On today’s show, Taxpayers for Common Sense President Steve Ellis, Stonecourt Capital Partner Rick Davis, Harvard Kennedy School Ash Center Visiting Democracy Fellow Jeanne Sheehan Zaino and Gulf Oil Chief Energy Advisor Tom Kloza. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Revives Tariff Agenda With Levies on EU, China
item.description: Bill Reinsch, senior advisor to the economic program at the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said that the new tariffs enacted by the Trump administration on the EU and China are 'pretty much the same' as the tariffs that were invalided by the Supreme Court. Reinsch said that it is too early to see real impacts from the Trump administration's tariff agenda other than higher prices on consumers. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pentagon Warns of Huge Fees If Congress Fails to Fund Munitions
item.description: The Trump administration is warning Congress that US taxpayers could be on the hook for billions of dollars in cancellation fees if lawmakers don’t fund massive munitions purchases aimed at rebuilding stockpiles drained by the Iran war.
item.dc:creator: Courtney McBride and Roxana Tiron

item.title: US Targets China, EU With New Tariffs Citing Overcapacity
item.description: The US announced plans to impose a fresh round of tariffs on goods from China, the European Union and a dozen other economies under President Donald Trump’s push to restore sweeping global import taxes that the Supreme Court found unconstitutional.
item.dc:creator: Alicia Diaz

item.title: Xi Unleashes China ‘Earthquake’ With Ouster of Rising Star
item.description: Ten months before his sudden downfall, Shanghai Party Chief Chen Jining made a visit to an industrial park incubating the city’s artificial intelligence start-ups.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
